_readme: DRAFT wording for the game. Rewrite freely. Every company name here is invented as a placeholder. Keep each id unique. A seller card needs id, name, tagline. A buyer card needs id, enterprise, title (need and incumbent.name are optional). 'rounds' must have one entry per round in js/config.js (game.rounds): 'title' is the round's name, 'new' is what changes (shown on the projector), 'buyer' and 'seller' are the one-line tips on the phones.
rules: Buyers: each round, stay with the supplier you have (safe), or sign a start-up. If it delivers you win big. If it fails, you answer for it.
Start-ups: get a buyer to type your deal code. Some of you have a product that is not ready. Nobody else knows which.
Three rounds of two minutes. After each one, the room sees who signed and who got burned.

rounds.title: Words only
rounds.new: Nothing but the pitch. Nobody can check anything.
rounds.buyer: You cannot check anything. Would you bet on a pitch?
rounds.seller: All you have is your pitch. Get a buyer to type your deal code.

rounds.title: Proof, and a small first step
rounds.new: A start-up with a reference customer can now prove it. And buyers may sign a small pilot instead of the full deal.
rounds.buyer: Type a deal code to see if that start-up has proof. Not sure? Sign a pilot: less to win, far less to lose.
rounds.seller: If you have proof, buyers see it when they type your code. If you do not, offer a pilot.

rounds.title: References and introductions
rounds.new: Everyone can now see what each start-up did in the earlier rounds. And every buyer knows the truth about one start-up.
rounds.buyer: Check a start-up's record before you sign. And look at who you know: you have the truth about one start-up.
rounds.seller: Your record is public now. Find the buyers who know you, and the ones you delivered for.

secret.ready: If a buyer signs you, you deliver.
secret.notReady: If a buyer signs you, you will fail to deliver. You still need the deal, so sell it anyway.
secret.proof: You have a reference customer. From round 2, a buyer who types your code sees that.
secret.noProof: You have no reference customer yet. From round 2 you can offer a pilot: a small first step is easier to say yes to.

buyerRule: Stay with your supplier and nothing can go wrong. Sign a start-up and you are the hero, or the one who answers for it.
